ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in parallelogram $ABCD$, $\angle ABC = 45^\circ$. Points $E$ and $F$ are located on the extensions of $CD$ and $BC$ respectively, with $AE \parallel BD$ and $\angle EFC = 30^\circ$. Given $AB = 1$, what is the length of $CF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw line EH $\perp$ BF at point H,\\
$\because$ Quadrilateral ABCD is a parallelogram,\\
$\therefore AB \parallel CD$, AB=DC,\\
$\because AE \parallel DB$,\\
$\therefore$ Quadrilateral ABDE is a parallelogram,\\
$\therefore AB=DE=CD$, thus D is the midpoint of CE.\\
$\because AB=1$,\\
$\therefore CE=2$,\\
$\therefore AB \parallel CD$,\\
$\therefore \angle ECF=\angle ABC=45^\circ$,\\
$\because CE=8$, $\angle ECF=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore EH=CH=\sqrt{2}$,\\
$\because \angle EFC=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore FH=\sqrt{3}EH=\sqrt{6}$,\\
$\therefore CF=\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{6}=\boxed{\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{6}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure it can be seen that B, C, F are on the same horizontal straight line, C is located between B and F, and F is on the right-side extension line of C; C, D, E are on the same oblique line, D is located between C and E, and E is on the extension line of CD; A, B, C, D form a parallelogram, and AE and BD are drawn, with the directions of the two lines parallel to each other. Reasoning: Since ABCD is a parallelogram, AB ∥ CD and CD = AB = 1 are obtained. Because E is on the extension line of CD, DE and CD are collinear, thus AB ∥ DE; also it is known that AE ∥ BD, therefore quadrilateral ABDE is a parallelogram, so DE = AB = 1. Thus CE = CD + DE = 1 + 1 = 2. Since CE and CD are on the same line, CF and BC are on the same line, and AB ∥ CD, ∠ECF = ∠ABC = 45°. In triangle ECF, it is known that ∠EFC = 30°, so ∠CEF = 180° - 45° - 30° = 105°. By the sine theorem, CF/sin105° = CE/sin30°, so CF = 2·sin105°/sin30° = 4sin105°. Also sin105° = sin(60°+45°) = (√6+√2)/4, therefore CF = √6 + √2.
